title: 1959 AHSME Problem 10
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) with \(\overline{AB}=\overline{AC}=3.6,\) a point \(D\) is taken on \(\overline{AB}\) at a distance \(1.2\) from \(A.\) Point \(D\) is joined to point \(E\) in the prolongation of \(\overline{AC}\) so that triangle \(AED\) is equal in area to triangle \(ABC.\) Then \(\overline{AE}\) equals:

solutions.text:
Triangles \(AED\) and \(ABC\) use bases on the same line \(AC.\) Since \[ \frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{1.2}{3.6}=\frac13, \] the perpendicular distance from \(D\) to line \(AC\) is one-third the corresponding distance from \(B.\) Equality of areas therefore requires \[ AE\left(\frac h3\right)=AC(h), \] so \(AE=3AC=10.8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Compare the altitudes from \(B\) and \(D\) to the line \(AC\)
Because \(\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{1}{3},\) the altitude from \(D\) is one-third the altitude from \(B\)
